name: Epoxy Resin & Epichlorohydrin: Domestic Chain Build-out Behind Anti-Dumping Duty
scope: India's epoxy chain (BPA + ECH -> liquid epoxy resin -> formulations): the November 2025 anti-dumping duty, new domestic ECH and resin capacity, and what it means for DCM Shriram, Grasim, Atul, Epigral and adjacent listed names.

summary.one_line: India now has about 152,000 tpa of commissioned ECH across three listed producers and a five-year duty on liquid epoxy resin, but the margin payoff has not shown up yet. Grasim reports compressed specialty margins, Epigral's resin entry is due only in H2 FY28, and BPA is still the missing domestic link.
key_points: Notification 33/2025-Customs (ADD), dated 17 Nov 2025, imposes duty of US$37-483/MT on liquid epoxy resin from China, Korea, Saudi Arabia, Taiwan and Thailand for five years. Solid, solution, waterborne, modified and brominated grades are excluded (S1).

DCM Shriram commissioned 35,000 tpa of glycerine-based ECH in Oct 2025 and the remaining 17,000 tpa on 1 Apr 2026, for 52,000 tpa in total (S2, S13). Grasim started commercial production at a 50,000 tpa ECH plant at Vilayat on 21 Oct 2026 (S3). The trade press reported that start on 15 Nov 2026 and said the plant uses captive chlorine (S4).

Grasim is already India's largest epoxy maker, with 246K TPA of epoxy resins and curing agents. Its FY26 annual report nevertheless describes 'a clear margin compression cycle' after the anti-dumping duty on ECH imports and the inverted duty structure created by the Korea FTA (S5).

Epigral's board approved a Rs 600 cr, 125,000 tpa epoxy resin and formulations plant at Dahej, targeted for H2 FY28 (S7). Over 50% of its raw-material value is to come from in-house sources (S8). A further 50,000 tpa of ECH, which doubles capacity to 100,000 tpa, was in trial runs at Q2 FY27 (S10, S11).

Atul added 50,000 tpa of liquid epoxy resin to a 30,000 tpa base, effective 25 Oct 2024 (S12). Atul and Hindusthan Speciality Chemicals were the petitioners in the resin anti-dumping case (S17). DCM Shriram has since agreed to buy Hindusthan Speciality Chemicals for Rs 375 cr (S14).
BPA is still the gap in the chain. The only filed Indian BPA project we found is Deepak Chem Tech's (Deepak Nitrite) board-approved plant of up to 240 KTA at about Rs 2,500 cr (S18).

Demand is growing but its size is not settled. Persistence Market Research estimates US$730.7m in 2025 at a 6.3% CAGR to 2032, with coatings at about 54.7% (S19). DCM Shriram management puts Indian demand at over 320,000 t a year (S13).
The market has not re-rated the theme. Epigral was down 38.5% over one year as of 12 Nov 2026 (S24) and Atul about 11% as of 28 Oct 2026 (S23).

for_investors.title: Who benefits
points: Integrated chlor-alkali players that can put chlorine into ECH and then resin: Grasim (S4, S5), DCM Shriram (ECH plus the HSCL resin plant) (S13, S14) and Epigral (S7, S8).
Existing liquid epoxy resin producers protected by the US$37-483/MT duty, mainly Atul and Grasim (S1, S12).
Epigral, if its 125,000 tpa resin plant is delivered. At Rs 600 cr the capex is about a quarter of its FY26 revenue of Rs 2,527 cr (S7, S11).

for_investors.title: Who is hurt / risks
points: The duty covers only liquid epoxy resin. Solid, solution, waterborne and modified grades stay open to imports (S1).

Downstream pass-through: the separate ECH duty (Notification 24/2024, up to US$557/MT) raised input costs for non-integrated resin makers. Grasim cites it, together with the Korea FTA inverted duty, for its compressed margins (S5, S15).
Atul's exports to the US carry US anti-dumping duty of 12.69% and countervailing duty of 10.66% (S16).
Epigral's EBITDA margin fell to 18% in Q2 FY27 from 23% on raw-material costs (S9). The resin plant is not due until H2 FY28 (S7).

for_investors.title: What to watch
points: Commissioning of Epigral's ECH (to 100,000 tpa) and CPVC expansion, guided for 'within the next quarter' at Q2 FY27 (S9, S10).
Utilisation of Grasim's 50,000 tpa ECH plant, which started on 21 Oct 2026 (S3).
DCM Shriram's next epoxy phase, guided for Q2 FY27 (S13); we found no commissioning filing.
Detailed engineering and a timeline for Deepak Chem Tech's BPA plant (S18).
Whether wind-blade demand picks up, e.g. the Grasim-Suzlon recyclable blade pilot (S21) and Inox Wind's new blade plant (S22).

kpis.label: Anti-dumping duty on liquid epoxy resin

subsections.title: The chain and its end markets

blocks.text: Liquid epoxy resin is made from bisphenol A (BPA) and epichlorohydrin (ECH), then formulated with hardeners or curing agents. Grasim's portfolio shows the downstream layers: liquid epoxy resins, formulated resins, reactive diluents and hardeners. These serve wind composites, automotive coatings, anti-corrosion systems, construction chemicals, electronics and packaging (S5). DCM Shriram management says ECH accounts for over 80% of global epoxy feedstock (S13). Its ECH uses refined glycerine rather than propylene and is integrated with its chlor-alkali operations (S13).

items: Coatings are the largest end use: Persistence Market Research estimates paints and coatings at about 54.7% of India's 2025 epoxy resin market (S19).
Grasim says epoxy demand is structurally supported by wind energy, e-mobility and infrastructure (S5).

Wind blades are a visible new demand node. Grasim, Aditya Birla Renewables and Suzlon signed an MoU in Nov 2026 to pilot blades made with Grasim's Recyclamine epoxy (S21), and Inox Wind is building a Rs 4 bn blade plant in Karnataka (S22).

subsections.title: Import dependence and the BPA gap

blocks.text: DCM Shriram management says India has traditionally relied heavily on imported ECH and high-purity epoxy intermediates (S13). The DGTR found that dumped liquid epoxy resin from China, Korea, Saudi Arabia, Taiwan and Thailand undercut domestic prices and caused material injury (S1). We could not confirm an official tonnage for imports of epoxy resin, ECH or BPA in this edition, so we leave those numbers out.

BPA is still the missing domestic link. The only filed Indian BPA project we found is Deepak Chem Tech's plant of up to 240 KTA (about Rs 2,500 cr, board approval 4 Aug 2026). Its main purpose is to feed Deepak's own polycarbonate plant, but it also targets Indian BPA demand, where epoxy is the main use (S18).

subsections.title: Two layers of trade protection: ECH (2024) and liquid epoxy resin (2025)

blocks.caption: Anti-dumping duty on liquid epoxy resin, Notification 33/2025-Customs (ADD), 17 Nov 2025 (S1)

items: The duty runs for five years from publication and is payable in rupees. It covers LER with an epoxy equivalent weight of 250 g/eq or less. Solid, semi-solid, solution, waterborne, blended or modified LER and brominated solvent epoxy are excluded (S1).
The duty also applies to subject-origin goods shipped via any third country, which partly addresses circumvention by transhipment (S1).
Petitioners were Atul and Hindusthan Speciality Chemicals. Epigral raised product-scope objections during the investigation (S17).
An earlier duty on ECH, Notification 24/2024-Customs (ADD) of 11 Nov 2024, covers China, Korea and Thailand at nil to US$557/MT for five years (S15).

blocks.text: The ECH duty helps ECH makers (Epigral, DCM Shriram, Grasim) but raises costs for resin makers that buy ECH. Grasim's FY26 annual report links a 'clear margin compression cycle' in specialty chemicals to the ECH anti-dumping duty and to the Korea FTA's inverted duty structure (S5).

blocks.text: Recent prints show no visible duty dividend yet. Grasim's chemicals EBITDA fell 11% YoY to Rs 326 cr in Q2 FY27, partly on weaker specialty chemicals profitability from high input prices and softer end-user demand (S6). Epigral grew Q2 FY27 revenue 28% to Rs 752 cr, but its EBITDA margin fell to 18% from 23% (S9). It ran ECH at 75-80% utilisation in the quarter (S10).

Beyond the four core names, the qualifying listed exposure is adjacent rather than pure-play: Deepak Nitrite (BPA) (S18), Pidilite (Araldite epoxy adhesives) (S20), and wind-blade makers Suzlon (S21) and Inox Wind (S22). Hindusthan Speciality Chemicals, Kukdo and Aditya Birla Chemicals (Thailand) are not listed in India. We found no listed small-cap Indian hardener, CCL or epoxy formulator with filed epoxy capacity plans, so Epigral is the only small/mid-cap pure exposure.

subsections.title: What forecasters and the market say

items: Persistence Market Research forecasts the India epoxy resin market growing from US$730.7m (2025) to US$1,120.7m by 2032, about 6.3% CAGR (S19).
Grasim management calls the medium- to long-term outlook constructive, but expects FY27 to stay volatile with near-term profitability uncertain (S5).
DCM Shriram's advanced-materials CEO targets optimal epoxy utilisation by 2030 (S13).
We found no broker note dedicated to the epoxy/ECH theme. Coverage is mostly trade press reporting company filings (S4, S9, S21).

blocks.text: The brief cites Epigral at about -44% over a year. The latest dated source we found shows -38.54% as of 12 Nov 2026 (S24). Either way, the stock has been de-rated rather than re-rated despite the duty and the epoxy plan.

items: Chinese oversupply and pricing: Grasim cites global oversupply and heightened competition as persistent near-term pressures on pricing and margins (S5).
Product-scope leakage: solid, solution, waterborne and modified epoxy fall outside the duty (S1).
Inverted duty: Grasim flags the Korea FTA's inverted duty structure as hurting specialty margins (S5).
Sunset: the resin duty runs until Nov 2030 and the ECH duty until Nov 2029, five years from 11 Nov 2024 (S1, S15). Investment cases assuming protection beyond that carry review risk.
Export barriers: Atul faces US anti-dumping duty of 12.69% and countervailing duty of 10.66% on epoxy resins (S16).

Execution: Epigral's resin plant is not due until H2 FY28 (S7), and its Q2 FY27 margins were hit by raw-material costs (S9). DCM Shriram's ECH uses refined glycerine rather than propylene, which exposes it to glycerine prices (S13).

companies.name: DCM Shriram Ltd
companies.role: Runs a 52,000 tpa glycerine-based ECH plant at Jhagadia, fully commissioned on 1 Apr 2026 and integrated with its chlor-alkali business (S2, S13). It is moving into resin through the Rs 375 cr acquisition of Hindusthan Speciality Chemicals, which has reported liquid epoxy resin capacity of over 17,000 tpa (S14).
companies.impact: Protected on both sides: the ECH duty shields its ECH (S15) and the resin duty shields its downstream resin (S1). Still small against FY26 revenue of Rs 14,264 cr (S25). Management targets optimal epoxy utilisation by 2030 (S13).

companies.name: Grasim Industries Ltd
companies.role: India's largest epoxy maker, with 246K TPA of epoxy resins and curing agents serving wind, coatings, construction and electronics (S5). It began commercial production at a 50,000 tpa ECH plant at Vilayat on 21 Oct 2026 (S3), next to its chlor-alkali and epoxy operations, using captive chlorine (S4).
companies.impact: The ECH plant removes exposure to dutiable imported ECH. Grasim blamed FY26 specialty margin compression on the ECH duty and the Korea FTA inverted duty (S5). Chemicals EBITDA fell 11% YoY in Q2 FY27 (S6). Epoxy is a small share of consolidated revenue (S6).

companies.name: Atul Ltd
companies.role: Liquid epoxy resin producer. It added 50,000 tpa to a 30,000 tpa base effective 25 Oct 2024 (S12) and was a lead petitioner in the resin anti-dumping case (S17).
companies.impact: Direct beneficiary of the US$37-483/MT duty on competing imports (S1). Its export route to the US is constrained by duties of 12.69% (anti-dumping) and 10.66% (countervailing) (S16). The stock was down about 11% over one year as of 28 Oct 2026 (S23).

companies.name: Epigral Ltd
companies.role: Chlor-alkali, ECH and CPVC producer. ECH capacity is going from 50,000 to 100,000 tpa (S11), with trial runs at Q2 FY27 (S10). Its board approved a Rs 600 cr, 125,000 tpa epoxy resin and formulations plant for H2 FY28 (S7), with over 50% of raw-material value from in-house sources (S8).
companies.impact: The only needle-mover in the group: epoxy capex is about a quarter of FY26 revenue (S7, S11). It was the applicant for the ECH duty (S15). Q2 FY27 margins fell to 18% (S9). The stock was down 38.5% over one year as of 12 Nov 2026 (S24).

companies.name: Deepak Nitrite Ltd
companies.role: Its subsidiary Deepak Chem Tech approved a BPA plant of up to 240 KTA at about Rs 2,500 cr in Aug 2026 to feed its polycarbonate plant and the Indian BPA market (S18).
companies.impact: The only filed project we found that would close the BPA gap in India's epoxy chain. Timing is not firm (S18).

companies.name: Pidilite Industries Ltd
companies.role: Owns the Araldite epoxy adhesives business, acquired from Huntsman's Indian subsidiary (S20).
companies.impact: A downstream formulator and resin buyer. The resin duty could raise input costs if domestic prices move toward landed import parity (S1).

companies.name: Suzlon Energy Ltd
companies.role: Wind turbine maker. It will manufacture recyclable blades with Grasim's Recyclamine epoxy under a Nov 2026 pilot MoU (S21).
companies.impact: Wind-blade demand is a growth driver for domestic epoxy. Suzlon aims to make all future turbines recyclable within three to four years (S21).

companies.name: Inox Wind Ltd
companies.role: Wind turbine maker building a Rs 4 bn blade manufacturing unit in Karnataka (S22).
companies.impact: New blade capacity adds domestic demand for epoxy composite systems. The plant was guided to start in 2026 (S22).

method: First edition, researched on 2026-11-19 with web search and page fetches. Primary documents were read directly where possible: the CBIC/MoF notification 33/2025 rate table, DCM Shriram's Reg 30 filing, Grasim's FY26 annual report chemicals chapter, the Aditya Birla Q2 FY27 release and the US ITA determination. Company events were cross-checked against trade press. Where a source shows no publication date (annual report chapter, press release, market-research and stock pages), the date field is the access date. The DGTR final-findings PDF was too large to fetch, so official import tonnages for epoxy, ECH and BPA are left out. Stock returns come from dated third-party quote pages and differ across providers. No ratings or price targets.
